On uninformative displays without an informative word, visual attention defaults to contextually unique singletons.

live.name: rsa_l1_singleton_feat_color_valence_l0
live.hypothesis: RSA pragmatic listener at depth 1 with singleton salience, contextual distinctiveness, visual feature complexity, evaluative valence framing, visual color contrast, and literal L0. Refining rsa_l2_singleton_feat_color_valence_l0 by reducing pragmatic recursion depth from depth 2 to depth 1: listeners interpret referring expressions by inverting an informative speaker who evaluates literal semantics, rather than engaging in higher-order recursive mental simulation. This bounded depth eliminates over-implicature in scalar implicature and prevents multiplicative prior compounding across reasoning tiers, preserving appropriate probability on multi-feature competitors while maintaining common knowledge of visual singleton salience, continuous contextual distinctiveness, valence-modulated feature complexity, and color contrast. Differences from rsa_l2_singleton_feat_color_valence_l0: recursion depth is reduced from depth 2 to depth 1 (listener calls L1 instead of L2), the depth-2 listener memo L2 is removed, and all parameters (alpha, w_singleton, w_distinct, w_features, w_valence, w_color) are preserved without addition or removal.

live.name: bounded_depth_feature_parsimony
live.hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions with strictly bounded reasoning depth (depth 1) by inverting an informative speaker over literal semantics, but penalize candidate referents possessing redundant visual features using a feature parsimony heuristic taken from feature_parsimony_listener. On informative trials, this parsimony penalty prevents visual singleton salience from spuriously overriding communicative informativeness for multi-feature competitors, while on uninformative displays visual attention defaults to contextually unique singletons. Differences from bounded_depth_listener: recursion depth remains depth 1 (listener calls L1); parameter beta is added with prior dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0); no parameters are removed (retaining alpha and w_singleton); L1 adds feature_count to its signature and scales referent choice weights by exp(-beta * vec(feature_count, r)); and listener passes beta and ctx.feature_count into L1 on informative trials.

live.name: feature_uncertainty_listener_2
live.hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions under referential feature uncertainty, being unsure which visual feature of a candidate referent the speaker intended to pick out. When evaluating literal semantics, listeners weight an object's compatibility by the probability that the speaker chose the heard feature from that object's feature bundle, naturally favoring minimal referents whose features are exhaustively described over cluttered multi-feature competitors. Communicative speakers select expressions expecting this feature-attribution inference, while spontaneous visual attention on uninformative displays defaults to contextually unique singletons.
